─── THE 6 ENTRIES BELOW ARE THE FIRST HONEST READING, 2026-08-12 ───────────
All six PREDATE this gate. Nothing got worse on the day it landed — the
instrument arrived. Every one lives in code owned by another lane, and this
gate's territory is tools/ only: a gate MEASURES, and when it finds defects it
REPORTS them. See `territory` on each entry for the routing.
S3 (2 entries) is the duplicate-store hazard BIM30-READINESS-GATES §3.2 names as
this gate's core subject, caught in its exact predicted shape: two live
singletons answering for one kind, DISAGREEING after real command seeding.
S1 + S4-VOICE (4 entries) are one mechanism seen from two ends: a bridge that
swallows its command's refusal and resolves the bus promise as success. The
refusal EXISTS and NAMES ITS RULE — it is emitted on a CustomEvent — it simply
never reaches the dispatch site. Success and refusal are the same observable to
the caller, which is the §CONTEXT-DATA-HONESTY failure this repo keeps paying
for: two very different facts printing the same value.
note2026-08-12-S4-VOICE-PAID: The THREE `S4-VOICE REFUSAL …(absent …)` entries are STRUCK — paid in this commit under §FIX-S4-VOICE-ABSENT-TARGET, per the both-directions rule in the header (debt that has been paid must LEAVE this file in the commit that pays it). Contract: C16 §5.1 CA-18 — 'REFUSE WITH A NAMED REASON, NEVER SUCCEED SILENTLY', whose prohibited shape (b) is exactly what these three did: `{forward:[],inverse:[]}` returned as the outcome of a mutation the user asked for. THE MECHANISM WAS NOT ONE BUG BUT TWO. (1) `wall.updateDimensions` (apps/editor/src/engine/initBusHandlers.ts) did its OWN existence check against the geometry `window.wallStore`, console.warn'd, and bare-`return`ed — the empty patch pair the bus read as success. It now THROWS a named refusal; the console.warn is KEPT, because the warn was never the defect, the return value was. (2) `roof.update` (same file) and `room.setName` (plugins/rooms/src/handlers/SetRoomName.ts) checked NOTHING and did not need to: `UpdateRoofCommand.canExecute` already refuses 'Roof not found' (UpdateRoofCommand.ts:27) and `RenameRoomCommand.canExecute` already refuses "Room '<id>' not found" (RenameRoomCommand.ts:39), and `CommandManagerImpl.execute` returns those verdicts as `{success:false, info:[reason]}` WITHOUT throwing (CommandManagerImpl.ts:172-185). Both call sites DISCARDED that object — `_cmExec` is even declared `: void`. They now read it and throw. WHY THROW AND NOT `canExecute {valid:false}`: existence is a GEOMETRY-STORE fact reachable only at execute time (the bridge's `validate(cmd)` is deliberately payload-shape-only and store-free; the plugin store does not hold detected rooms, as SetRoomName's own canExecute comment states), so canExecute could not have been the home. Throwing is also the shape the repo ALREADY pins — apps/editor/__tests__/RoofUpdateReachesGeometryStore.test.ts:160 asserts `rejects.toThrow()` for a refused roof.update, plugins/rooms CreateRoom.ts:196 reads `{success:false}` and throws, and every live call site already terminates in `.catch(...)` (RoofPropertySheet.ts:318, PropertyInspectorApply.ts:210/:234/:552, RoomPropertySection.ts:66/:973). BLAST RADIUS HELD DELIBERATELY NARROW: `_cmExec` has 90 call sites in initBusHandlers.ts; rather than make all 90 throw on a legacy failure — a behaviour change across ~40 verbs that no measurement here covers — a narrow sibling `_cmExecOrRefuse` was added and only `roof.update` adopts it. Widening that is its own lane with its own proof. S4-STATE passed on all three throughout: nothing was ever mutated, so the model was never at risk; the defect was purely that success and refusal were the same observable at the dispatch site. PROOF, EXECUTED: apps/editor/__tests__/bridgeRefusalReachesTheCaller.test.ts (10 cases, driving the REAL exported `initBusHandlers` exactly as certification/world.ts:203-204 does, not a hand-modelled bridge) plus 3 new room.setName cases in plugins/rooms/__tests__/handlers.test.ts. Each assertion is on the DISCRIMINANT (rejected vs resolved) and on the reason text naming the missing element — never on 'it did not throw'. Every suite was NEGATIVE-TESTED by reverting the fix: 5 of 10 editor cases and 2 of 3 rooms cases FAIL without it, and the cases that still pass are exactly the success-path ones — which is the evidence that zero behaviour changed when the element EXISTS.
